DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION
August 6, 1973
IN REPLY REFER TO
Mr. James Corbin, Director
Community Development Disaster
Recovery Office
Department of Housing and Urban
Development
Lackawanna County Building
Spruce and Adams Avenue
Scranton, Pennsylvania 18503
Re: Draft Environmental Impact Statement Penn-Susquehanna Urban Renewal Project Harrisburg, Pennsylvania HUD Project No. PA-R-634C
Dear Mr. Corbin:
As regards the above referenced subject we submit the following:
1. Our Engineering District Office reviewed the Draft EIS and provided specific comments and suggestions as per the enclosed letter. We concur with and endorse fully these comments and suggestions.
2. We further submit the following comments in addition to the District's: 
a. We disagree with the project's basic objective which is to eliminate or lessen the suffering and damage caused by the storm. The fact is that even before the big flood the Penn-Susquehanna neighborhood could already be considered as blighted and deteriorated area which could easily qualify for rehabilitation under the Federal Urban Renewal Program. The damage wrought by Agrees has been relieved to a considerable extent as attested by the number of individuals and businesses who have received S.B.A. recovery assistance. (2. Objectives, page 11)
b. It is true that the use of the River Front Park by both project residents and outsiders is particularly high in the summer months. The Park runs a distance of 40 blocks along Front Street. Pedestrian access to the Park, however, is a problem. The only way to get to the Park is by crossing Front Street which carries heavy, fast moving traffic. (4. Recreation, page 36)
